Sir George Williams University 
Alumni participation in the 


$7,CCO,000 Building Fund HARRY THOMAS 


FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE 

Sir George Williams University Alumni leaders 
have undertaken to obtain full participation and significant fin- 
ancial support from members in their Alma Mater's $7,000,000 
national appeal for funds to complete financing of a new $23,900,000 
building. The organization of such an effort is not an easy assignment. 

In the Montreal area alone, some ),000 Sir George 
alumni reside. Plans are underway to carry out a personal canvass 
of each Montreal alumnus. It will take place during May. 

In addition to the local alumni campaign another 
1,200 members will be contacted by mail or by personal contact, 
where possible, in major Canadian, U.S. and World centers. Sir 
George alumni live in every Canadian province, in a majority of 
States in the U.S. and e every continent. 

The canvass of Montreal alumni members will be 
carried out om a geographical basis. The City has beon divided 
into areas; each area chairman will select team eaptains who in 
turn will form canvassing teams. 

Theodore D. (Ted) Lande, Vice-President and 
General Manager of Community Finance Corp., Alumni. c=mp3ign chair- 
man, feels strongly that Sir George graduates will enthusiastically 


support this appeal if they are fully informed about the University's 


plans and the great need that must be met. For this reason it is 
important to have the cooperation of press media to help us reach 
our Alumni who have so dispersed throughout the community. 
Associate chairmen of the Alumni campaign are 
Jean J. Des Rosiers, Vice-President of Armand Des Rosiers Inc.; 
Charles Nichols, President of Woco Yarss; Ernest Brown, Secretary- 


Treasurer of Dominion Flour Co., and John R. Hannon.

HARRY THOMAS 


L'Association des Anciens de 1'Université Sir George 
Williams tentera d'obtenir la participation de tous ses membres 
de méme qu'un support financier sans préeédent, afin de contribuer 
au succés de la campagne de souscription de l'Université Sir 


Beorge Williams. 


La direction de la campagne des anciens prépare un 
appel personnel, plusieurs anciens solliciteront leurs quelques 
4,000 confréres qui demeurent 4 Montréal et les environs. Les 


autres seront approchés par correspondance. 


Pour les fins de la campagne, on divisera la ville 
en plusieurs secteurs géographiques. D'ici peu, plusieurs anciens 
seront approchés afin de former des 4quipes, puisque la sollicita- 
tion aura lieu au mois de mai. On se souviendra que l'objectif 
total de la campagne est de $7,000,000 et que le coiit de l'édifice 


est de $23,000,000 


M. Ted Lande espére compter sur la collaboration de 
taus les anciens et des journalistes Montréalais. Pour toute 
autre information veuillez communiquer avec M. J. Ferguson 4 


VI.4-0131, poste téléphonique 51.
